Container.Name: kb-webui
Container.Overview: Open WebUI - the chat window over the shared knowledge library. STARTED IN ORDER: kb-postgres first, then kb-service, then kb-webui. There is no template equivalent of compose depends_on, so nothing enforces that for you. NETWORK: the kb containers share one user-defined Docker network named kb that you create once, by hand, before the first start (a template cannot create a network, so Network stays bridge here - set it to kb when you create the container). Docker must preserve user-defined networks across updates (Unraid: Settings > Docker, Preserve user defined networks = Yes), or the containers fall back to bridge and the container names stop resolving. EXPOSURE: this container is exposed on your LAN through the host port you choose; unlike kb-postgres it is meant to be reached from the wider network. Anything further (a domain, reverse proxy, TLS) is a separate step for whoever administers your network. COOKIES: the UI is served over plain HTTP, so the secure-cookie setting ships off; turn WEBUI_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE on when a TLS front end exists, or login breaks the other way round. ACCOUNTS: authentication is on and sign-up is off; the first administrator is created on the first visit to an empty database, after which registration stays closed. STORAGE: the data mount holds the chat database and uploaded files - put it under backup. The update check and the analytics switches are off. IMAGE TAG: pinned to one release; an Update is a deliberate bump of that pin.
Container.Description: Open WebUI chat window over the knowledge library. Start this last. LAN-exposed; set a free host port and a secret key.

Config.Name: HTTP Port
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Host port for the web UI; the container always listens on 8080 internally - change the host side only. No default is offered because 8080 is taken on the usual host: pick a free port.

Config.Name: Data
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Chat database, uploaded files and model caches. Set an absolute path on a POOL, e.g. /mnt/<pool>/appdata/kb-webui/data. Put it under backup.

Config.Name: WEBUI_SECRET_KEY
Config.Description: REQUIRED. Signing key for login sessions; the app refuses to start with authentication on and no key. Use a long random value and keep it stable - changing it signs everyone out.

Config.Name: ENABLE_SIGNUP
Config.Description: Allow self-registration. false: only the first administrator, created on an empty database, and accounts an administrator adds.

Config.Name: WEBUI_SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE
Config.Description: Mark the login cookies Secure. false while the UI is served over plain HTTP (a Secure cookie is never sent over HTTP and login fails). Set true when a TLS front end exists.

Config.Name: OLLAMA_BASE_URL
Config.Description: Ollama endpoint, format http://<host>:<port> . Blank: the app falls back to its own built-in address, which reaches nothing useful from this container.

Config.Name: OPENAI_API_BASE_URL
Config.Description: OpenAI-compatible endpoint, format http://<host>:<port>/v1 . Blank: the app falls back to the public OpenAI address, which without a key does nothing.

Config.Name: OPENAI_API_KEY
Config.Description: Key for the OpenAI-compatible endpoint above. Blank if the endpoint takes none.

Config.Name: ENABLE_VERSION_UPDATE_CHECK
Config.Description: Ask the upstream project whether a newer version exists. false: no outbound check.

Config.Name: SCARF_NO_ANALYTICS
Config.Description: Opt out of Scarf package analytics. Leave true.

Config.Name: DO_NOT_TRACK
Config.Description: Standard do-not-track switch read by bundled libraries. Leave true.

Config.Name: ANONYMIZED_TELEMETRY
Config.Description: Anonymized usage telemetry of the bundled vector-store library. Leave false.
